title: Reconstruction Payment Desk Policy: Draw Payments, Mortgagee Releases and Insurance Postings
content:
The contract balance of a Reconstruction contract is the amount the customer owes on that one contract: charges raise it; draw payments, insurance postings and deductive change order credits lower it.

## Rules in force

1. **Contract status.** The contract must not be closed or cancelled when a draw payment or insurance posting is recorded.
2. **Tenders.** Draws are paid by debit card, ACH, check or wire, and mortgagee releases arrive as mortgagee checks; credit cards are not accepted on Reconstruction contracts.
3. **Same claim file.** The carrier payment must be recorded on the same claim file this contract is linked to.
4. **Which carrier payments are posted.** Only dwelling-coverage carrier payments that reached the company directly, or by a two-party check the insured has endorsed, are posted to the contract, and only toward a carrier-direct draw.
5. **Once per contract.** A carrier payment is posted to the same contract at most once.
6. **Amount posted.** The amount posted is the least of the draw's unpaid amount, the contract balance and the carrier payment's unapplied remainder after every posting already made from it to any water, fire, mold or rebuild job, after the mitigation jobs of the claim file have been paid first under the claim payment allocation rule.

Rules 1, 3 and 5 are read from the company's records before the posting: the contract's status, the claim file the carrier payment is recorded on, and the postings already made from that carrier payment to this contract.

## Clause no longer in force

"Each payment names the one draw it pays and is posted in full to the contract." — no longer in force; superseded by the current payment basis.

## Posting an insurance payment: worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

A carrier-direct draw has $9,000.00 unpaid; the contract balance is $14,500.00; a dwelling payment of $20,000.00 reached the company directly, $12,600.00 of it is already posted to the claim file's mitigation jobs, which are paid in full. The unapplied remainder is $7,400.00, the least of the three figures, so $7,400.00 is posted toward the draw.

| Carrier payment | Posted to the contract? |
|---|---|
| Dwelling coverage, reached the company directly | Yes, toward a carrier-direct draw |
| Dwelling coverage, two-party check the insured has endorsed | Yes, toward a carrier-direct draw |
| Dwelling coverage, two-party check not endorsed | No |
| Recorded on a different claim file | No |
| Already posted once to this contract | No |

superseded_clauses: Each payment names the one draw it pays and is posted in full to the contract.
